Class PathGenerator

Return an object that is used to generate 3-tuple (startNodeIndex, edgeSequence, endNodeIndex), referred to as path-tuple for each valid path of a railyard.

The path-tuple of a path (startNodeIndex, edgeSequence, endNodeIndex) specifies the start node index (of the first edge), the sequence of edges and the end node index (of the last edge) of the path.

Attributes:

  • railyard: The railyard where the path-tuples are generated.
  • graph: The graph of railyard.
  • startNodeIndex: The start node index of a path-tuple, i.e. the start nodex index that connects to the first edge of edgeSequence.
  • edgeSequence: The edges inside of a path.
  • endNodeIndex: The end node index of a path-tuple, i.e. the end node index of the last edge of edgeSequence.
  • visited: The set of nodes visited when generating a path-tuple.

__init__(self, railyard, noPrefix=False, noSuffix=False, branch=True, posOrient=None)
(Constructor)

 

Constructor.

Parameters:
  • railyard (IRailyard) - The railyard where the path-tuples are generated.
  • noPrefix (bool) - If true, there is only one end node index in edgeSequence. That is, there is no more than one edge in edgeSequence that ends in a node index which is considered as end node index by the method isEndNodeIndex.
  • noSuffix (bool) - If true, there is only one start node index in edgeSequence. That is, there is no more than one edge in edgeSequence that starts in a node index which is considered as start node index by the method isStartNodeIndex.
  • branch (bool) - If true, branching is allowed when generating the path-tuple for a path traversing a node with degree bigger than 2.
  • posOrient (bool | none) - If true, only the paths whose oritantions are positive will be considered when generating the corresponding path-tuples. If false, only the paths whose orientations are not positive will be considered. An argument of None is interpreted as "no restriction".
Returns: none

isEdge(self, processedNodeIndex, newNodeIndex)

 

A callback function that determines if the edge from processedNodeIndex to newNodeIndex is a valid edge.

This function is called before the new edge is (conditionally) added. Subclasses may override this function to implement other specific conditions to determine if the edge is valid.

Parameters:
  • processedNodeIndex (NodeIndex) - The start node index that connects to the edge to be determined as a valid edge.
  • newNodeIndex (NodeIndex) - The end node index that connects to the edge to the edge to be determined as a valid edge.
Returns: bool
Return true if the edge is valid.
